entries.title: Maryland 38, UConn 14: Game Recap
entries.summary: The Terps' Malik Washington and Harry Dalton III lead Maryland to a win.
entries.content:
EAST HARTFORD, Conn. (AP) — Maryland is benefiting from their up-tempo offense in 2026.

The Terps scored 62 points in their season opening win over Hampton and rolled to a 38-14 win over Connecticut on Saturday in front of 34,494 fans at Pratt and Whitney Stadium.

After the host Huskies took a 7-0 lead in the first quarter, the Terrapins (2-0) scored on six of their next eight drives with five touchdowns and a field goal.

Maryland sophomore QB Malik Washington completed 34-of-41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns while Harry Dalton III ran for 48 yards and two touchdowns for the Terps.

“I am proud of this team. I told them this would be an audit for us,” Maryland coach Michael Locksley said. “I thought we did a good job of taking care of business. Malik was really efficient today.”

Washington, who completed 18 passes in a row at one point, completed passes to eight different receivers. Chris Durr Jr. pulled in a career-high 10 receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown. Na’eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding caught eight passes for a game-high 130 yards and a touchdown.

“We’re always going to be a multi-tempo offense,” Lockley said. “With us and a guy like Malik getting him in the rhythm is really important. It is more flow than tempo.

“There will be times we want to play fast and keep people off the field in certain situations. But I think our goal is to get 80 plays and the only way you can get 80 plays in today’s game is you have to go with some tempo,” he said. “When you have as many playmakers as we have on offense and the diversity of how we spread the ball around, you won’t get enough plays if you play slow.”

The Terps ran 78 plays on Saturday.

UConn (1-1) was led by QB Kalieb Osborne, who completed 10 of 21 passes for 156 yards with two touchdowns. He was UConn’s leading rusher with 30 yards on 13 carries. Maryland limited the Huskies to 67 yards on 31 carries.

Washington completed 16 of his first 16 passes in the second half for 138 yards and a touchdown as he marched the Terps up and down the field.

Streaks

Maryland has won 20 straight non-conference games. It is the longest streak in the FBS.

The loss to Maryland snapped a nine-game winning streak at Pratt and Whitney Stadium for the Huskies, dating back to a loss to Wake Forest in October 2024.

Up next

Maryland: vs. Virginia Tech next Saturday

entries.title: D.C. United 0, Atlanta United 0: Game Recap
entries.summary: Sean Johnson has two saves for a 0-0 tie with Atlanta.
entries.content:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Sean Johnson had two saves Saturday night for D.C. United in a 0-0 tie with Atlanta United.

The 37-year-old Johnson has six shutouts this season for D.C. United (6-7-11), which beat Columbus 2-1 on Wednesday night to snap a five-game winless streak.

Atlanta (6-14-5) is winless in four straight following a season-high three wins in a row.

Atlanta had 62% possession and outshot D.C. 18-4, 3-0 on target. D.C. had just one shot in the second half.

The teams also played to a scoreless tie March 21 in Atlanta.

entries.title: Nationals 6, Angels 5: Game Recap
entries.summary: Nats beat Angels despite another bullpen collapse.
entries.content:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Andrew Alvarez pitched seven innings of one-hit ball and the Washington Nationals earned a 6-5, 10-inning victory over the Los Angeles Angels on Saturday when CJ Abrams scored on an error despite another bullpen collapse.

Andrés Chaparro's single off Ben Joyce tied it in the ninth. Abrams scored against José Fermín (4-3) when shortstop Zach Neto could not handle Harry Ford's grounder with the infield in.

Before that, the Angels rallied to a 5-4 lead while handing Washington’s bullpen an MLB record-extending 39th blown save. Vaughn Grissom connected for a two-run homer during a three-run eighth against Brad Lord, and Wade Meckler, Denzer Guzman and Moisés Ballesteros also had RBIs.

Jack Sinclair (1-0) retired four batters for his first career win.

Washington's Abimelec Ortiz hit a two-run single during a three-run second. Jacob Young and Keibert Ruiz also drove in runs to help Washington to a 4-0 lead that Alvarez held as he departed.

Los Angeles sank to 4-14 in extra innings games this season.

Alvarez struck out a career-best eight batters — including three-time MVP Mike Trout twice — while working around four walks and Jose Siri’s sixth-inning double inside the left-field line.

The 27-year-old threw 61 of 97 pitches for strikes in his 20th and longest career start, retiring 13 of the last 14 batters he faced.

Previously, Alvarez carried a no-hitter into the fifth inning of his MLB debut on Sept. 1, 2025 against Miami.
